Thanks for doing this!

Can you move under docs/ ?
https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/master/docs/

repitition, how about 
"dbus associations to link"
remove that, either you know whats described in the document, then fine, otherwise you need to read it anyway to understand whats going on here.
Do you refer to the term in the redfish specification? If so, clarify this, otherwise its "computer system"
I do refer to the actual redfish resource. I have added a sentence at the top of the document, to emphasize that.

"Most associations needed are not in place yet"|

It should follow a list of the missing associations.
The missing associations should be inferred from the implemented section.
The proposal for the interface came from the mailing list
The interface determine the root element in redfishs's ComputerSystem (system name) tree.
I think root element is the wrong term here. I have called it redfish identifier for now to keep it simple. Is that ok?
As said above, I am referring to the actual rf resource.
Let's not write down what `redfish-system-uri-name` defaults to, people can look that up in `meson.options`.
As said above, I am referring to the actual rf resource.

Can we be a little more specific here to differentiate between this and aggregation?  I'm having a little trouble wordsmithing it, but something like "bmcs which directly manage multiple processor complexes"
Remove.  This sentence adds no value to this document.

Remove before this merges.  If it helps you, that's great, but pretty much every markdown renderer we have handles this already, and this doc shouldn't be unique in that regard.

Also, maintaining a correct TOC seems like something I don't personally want to take on for all the docs.
Remove all this.  This is great discussions happened, but this documentation needs to stand alone and survive longer than discord chats.

Remove.  OpenBMC hasn't been able to define the term "reference platform" well in an open source context, and I don't want to make it seem like "if it doesn't work on YT4 we won't accept your patch" which is generally how reference platforms work in corporations.
nit, use bottom links for these to keep the reading smooth.  Put the link at the bottom with a number or id, and only link the id here.
Inline links are being used in other docs too. It might keep reviewing smooth, but I don't think a reader of the doc would agree jumping around the document.
Also markdown-lint complains about bare urls.
Please use authoritative language "we want to use" should be changed to "bmcweb uses"

Remove.  We can point to code here, but we shouldn't point to a point-in-time gerrit review.  We should point to docs/code on master.

Also, at this level, dbus is supposed to be an abstraction, so I would remove reference to any specific daemon.

I'm going to stop reviewing at this point, because this is reading like a story, and not documentation on intent/design.  I realize it's WIP, so I'm assuming you're going to give a heavy scrub through for extra information.  From my read, this doc is probably 2X longer than it needs to be, and goes into things that aren't multi-host specific.  For example, there is already a Testing doc, so if everyone is expected to test multi-host things, that's where the testing documentation goes.

We can and should write this as what exists today in this design, and more importantly, how we expect new features to be implemented.
Thanks for your review. I tried to be precise with my language in this patchset.
Comes from D-Bus. It could be another backend. Oh well, Entity Manager is the only that supports it today.
I rephrased it a little bit, to indicate potential for change.

Started from the bottom. 

Can you remove these ? Other .md don't have them. 

Maybe just remove this whole testing section
Can you combine these in some way? It just repeats..
Can we combine the Processor collection and Processor ? Otherwise it just repeats
Aren't we moving away from Power to PowerSubsystem ? Can we just remove ? I know everyone doesn't use NMI
Why do you need these --- I don't see them other places. I don't see where a horizontal line helps
In general I had them in to increase readability. Should look ok now without. Done

This document provides 

or 

This document shall provide
Nitpick: to avoid introducing subtle bugs
Nitpick: Redfish like you do other places
shouldn't this be ### like Logging. I think it is under Not Implemented

bmcweb. But where in the Redfish does it say EventLog should be under ComputerSystem? Redfish allows for it under ComputerSystem or Manager.. 

I think these 2 paragraphs could be 2 sentence.
Also I don't know if you really need a work-arounds section, just put above. 

```
Ideally, EventLog responses would be scoped to the requested ComputerSystem, but bmcweb doesn’t currently support filtering EventLog entries by host. As a workaround, the redfish-eventlog-location=managers meson option moves the EventLog tree under /redfish/v1/Managers/{managerId}, providing a way to access logs on multi-host platforms.
```

Yea you are right, I think I got the wrong idea from a past discussion, without checking back with the spec.

I followed your suggested wording and got rid of the Work-around section. The EventLog under Managers got moved to the Implemented section under Logging. Done
